handback.t:
W20 (SONA-A) final report. All numbers are SYNTHETIC-until-validated-on-real-traffic. src/*.rs is untouched; I only added files under src/bin and results.

**Verdict.** SonaPlus is improved only in one narrow, author-built class of worlds. Evidence-gated, set-level (conjunction) pattern memory, placed behind the unchanged `defaults::recommended_guard()`, beats the best fair baseline where the best agent depends on feature conjunctions. It is harmless in my 6 control worlds. It is a loss in additive many-surface-form worlds. Learned anchors, kNN blending, consolidation and credit-with-the-SONA-estimator add nothing measurable over simpler alternatives in normal feedback.

**Mechanism that works ("K-full").** `HybridInner` trains hebbian-robust and `KeyedMemory` on every outcome. The decision comes from the memory only when its set-level evidence for the task's key reaches `min_w`; otherwise hebbian-robust decides. Evidence is the exact key-set pattern weight plus a Jaccard-weighted blend of the k=3 nearest patterns. Seeds 1-8 tuning chose min_w=3. The gate is what makes it safe in controls.

**Results (Holm, paired 95% CI, vs best of the 6 spec baselines, H2000):**

| Block | Worlds with Holm WIN | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 31-60 | conj-clean +0.038, conj-noisy +0.020, conjT-clean +0.064, shortmod-traps +0.034, shortmod-clean +0.049 | conjT-noisy +0.003 n.s. |
| 61-90 (fresh, frozen tuning) | same 5 worlds: +0.038, +0.020, +0.068, +0.038, +0.054 | |
| 91-120 (fresh, post-hoc min_w=8) | conj-clean +0.041, conj-noisy +0.021, conjT-clean +0.065, shortmod-clean +0.043 | shortmod-traps +0.017 n.s. |

- **Direct K-full minus guarded-safe (Holm wins/losses of 75 cells):** 20/7 (31-60) and 24/6 (61-90). With min_w=8 on 91-120: 18/3.
- **Controls:** no Holm loss vs the best baseline in any of var-single, traps(main), correct-keywords, many-topics(16), sim-random, sim-notraps, in all blocks. The ungated memory is not harmless: it loses in correct-keywords and sim-notraps, although its conjunction wins are larger.
- **Ablation (normal feedback has no reuse signal, so no confound):** K[anchors+hebbian], which is the same guard and anchors with no pattern memory, is equal to guarded-safe and has 0 wins in all blocks. Per-feature (unigram) pattern memory has 5 wins / 22 losses vs best-of-6; K-full minus it is 28 wins / 1 loss on 31-60 and 30 wins / 0 losses on 61-90. Only the set-level key helps, which re-confirms the D7 finding for per-feature memory.
- **Weak feedback, all arms fed the same reuse signal:** K-full[reuse] beats the strict pool only in weak-shortmod-traps (+0.044 / +0.056 at H2000). The large gains vs raw-fed baselines (e.g. +0.106 in weak-var-traps) are the reuse signal, as in D7.

**Negatives, stated plainly.**
- The wins exist only where I built conjunction structure. Five winning worlds come from two generators, not real data.
- conjT-*, var-wide and shortmod-* were added after seeing round-1/round-4 results.
- Frozen K-full loses 0.011-0.017 at H2000 in var-traps, var-clean and var-wide-traps (Holm p ≤ 1e-3 in both fresh blocks).
- min_w=8 reduces that loss to about 0.00-0.005 on 31-60, 61-90 and 91-120. It is a post-hoc one-factor choice made after the sensitivity table; var-clean is still a Holm loss of -0.005 on 91-120.
- In the trap-keyword conjunction worlds (conjT-*), K-full loses early (H100-H250) by 0.04-0.10 to eps-greedy/hebbian-robust. That is the keyword guard (guarded-safe has the same deficit), not the memory.
- **Learned anchors:** neutral in normal feedback (K-full minus no-anchors: 1 win / 0 losses and 3 / 1). Under sparse feedback they add +0.017 to +0.028 at H2000 (4 wins / 0 losses in both blocks). Clustering purity is 1.00 in `--diag-anchors`, but permissive thresholds cost 0.002-0.006 at H2000 in controls. The oracle-anchor diagnostic shows headroom for semantic anchors, which `knowledge.rs` could supply with real embeddings; I did not test that.
- **Consolidation:** with 16 patterns instead of 1161, importance-merge keeps ~45% of the memory's gain (0.5018 vs 0.5325 uncapped, guarded-safe 0.4765), while LRU/FIFO keep none (0.476-0.479). It never beats uncapped.
- **Trajectory credit** (posterior blame split in session worlds): a large generic gain for every router (guarded-safe 0.535 → 0.712 in sess-traps at H2000). The SONA pattern-memory estimator is worse than a plain per-feature estimator (0 wins / 10-12 losses), and no K arm beats the credit-fed baselines. This is not SONA-specific.

**Process.** The worlds and candidate went through 5 rounds, each with changes made after seeing 31-60 results; all five rounds are listed in the board entry (rounds 1-4 logs kept in `results/` but not reproducible by the final binary). 61-90 was frozen-tuning fresh seeds, and 91-120 was an extra fresh block.

**Checks.**
- AnchorGuard with anchors off is bit-identical to `defaults::recommended_router` (selfcheck max |diff| = 0).
- 3 unit tests pass.
- Repeat runs give identical JSON.

**Rerun (all of it, ~12-15 min per tuning run on 2 threads):** `bash results/g19a_run_all.sh`. The exact per-block commands are in the board entry's VERIFY REQUEST blocks.
